headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from Copilot-to-plano handoff; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Copilot reads repo context and open editor buffers, while plano only exposes an OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint and config files. No shared clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented, so direct injection is not default. The remaining pathway is manual or orchestrated handoff, which is lower blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator copies Copilot output into plano prompts without review, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared workspace or clipboard bridge is added, the risk increases.
mitigations: Review any Copilot-generated text before pasting into plano.
Disable shared clipboard between the two tools.
Use a fixed prompt template for plano inputs.
Keep plano prompts free of raw code or instructions from Copilot.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Copilot touches source code and open editor buffers, and plano touches logs, traces, metrics, and agentic signals. Even without a documented shared filesystem, a manual or pipeline handoff can move sensitive code or operational data between them. Because both can send data to vendor endpoints, the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF Copilot output includes secrets or proprietary code and is forwarded into plano prompts, leakage occurs.
IF plano logs are retained with copied Copilot context, sensitive data persists in logs.
mitigations: Redact secrets before any handoff.
Limit plano prompts to summaries, not raw code.
Turn off verbose logging for plano sessions.
Use separate workspaces for code and travel-planning tasks.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on prompt inputs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Copilot can write the filesystem and modify git state, while plano only shows config-file I/O and broad network egress. There is no evidence that both write the same mutable resource or share locks, so direct write-write conflict is not established. Uncertainty is limited, but not enough to raise severity.
conditions: IF plano is configured to edit the same repository or config directory Copilot is modifying, conflicts can occur.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable file set without locking, overwrites are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Pause one agent while the other writes.
Use git status before and after Copilot edits.
Keep plano read-only for shared files.
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Copilot can propose edits for human review, and plano can consume chat-completion inputs and emit routing or planning outputs. If Copilot-generated facts or code are forwarded into plano without verification, plano may amplify errors into downstream actions or logs. The pairwise handoff is plausible, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Copilot output is treated as authoritative input to plano, errors can cascade.
IF plano uses unverified Copilot-generated facts in routing or planning decisions, downstream mistakes increase.
mitigations: Require a human verification step between agents.
Ask plano to cite sources independently.
Use Copilot only for drafts, not final facts.
Keep plano outputs advisory unless reviewed.
requires-engineering: add validation checks between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Copilot is tied to GitHub repo context and open buffers, while plano touches logs and metrics. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, so a compliance breach is not established. The main concern is accidental logging of code or operational traces, which is limited and controllable.
conditions: IF Copilot-derived code is copied into plano logs, retention policy mismatch may matter.
IF plano is deployed in a jurisdiction with stricter logging rules, compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in plano prompts.
Minimize retention on plano logs.
Review GitHub repo access scopes.
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention policies.
